text:
anna: hello team, first-week newbie here. I just demoed a quick prototype and accidentally used a hosted API key on my laptop. During the demo we hit a bunch of 429s and then after I rotated the key my scripts started returning 401. quick q: should new hires ever use hosted keys locally? and what's the fastest way to avoid 429s while iterating? :grimacing:

chris: welcome! :wave: short: avoid hosted keys for local/dev. Use a sandbox key for day-to-day work. Hosted keys = production, higher quota but sensitive and billed. Sandbox keys are intended for experiments and onboarding.

anna: where can I create a sandbox key? i only saw "Hosted API Key" at first in Console.

devon: Console -> API keys -> Create sandbox key. SSO/role provisioning can take a couple minutes after you join. If it's missing, ping #devex and include your org handle.

chris: to reduce 429s while you iterate: 1) local throttling (sleep/jitter between calls), 2) exponential backoff honoring Retry-After header, 3) mock the API for unit tests, 4) request a short-lived CI sandbox key for integration tests.

anna: is there a template for the CI sandbox/quota request?

devon: yes, post in #devex with: "Quota/key request - repo:<repo>, purpose:<CI|staging|pairing>, expected RPS:<n>, duration:<24h|72h>, contact:@<handle>". Example: "Quota/key request - repo:search-ui, purpose:CI integration, expected RPS:5, duration:48h, contact:@anna"

anna: rotation order question: I created a new hosted key in Console, but forgot to update GitHub Actions secrets and my worker kept using the old value -> 401s. what's the right sequence?

chris: recommended sequence: 1) create new key (Console), 2) update secrets store (Vault/GH secrets/etc), 3) restart/deploy services so they pick up the new secret, 4) verify success, 5) revoke old key. If your service caches env at start, restart it.

anna: thanks. any headers to look at when debugging 429s?

devon: watch X-RateLimit-Remaining, X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Reset and Retry-After if present. Logging these helped us trace which tests or jobs are burning quota.

ops-bot: :info: Tip: for quick local calls you can set env var temporarily: `export REDWOOD_API_KEY="<sandbox-key>"` and curl with `-s` for small loops. Do not commit env files.

infra-bot: :warning: Security reminder: do NOT commit hosted API keys. If a key is exposed, rotate immediately and notify security@redwood.ai. Automated scanners may flag commits.

anna: all good now 44d switched to sandbox for local dev, opened a #devex request for a 48h CI sandbox key for our integration tests, and added basic backoff. saved the checklist, thanks everyone! :thumbsup:
